problem: Given that the distance from a point $P$ to the origin is $7,$ and that $P$ makes an angle of $0$ with the positive $x$-axis, what are the Cartesian coordinates of $P?$
worked_solution:
We notice that the point $P$ is described using polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ where

$$
r=7,\,\theta =0.
$$

To convert from polar coordinates to Cartesian coordinates, we use

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

First, we calculate the $x$-coordinate of $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ x & =7\operatorname{cos}⁡(0) \\ x & =7\cdot 1 \\ x & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the $y$-coordinate of $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ y & =7\operatorname{sin}⁡(0) \\ y & =7\cdot 0 \\ y & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are $(7,0).$
